title: Someone is hurt or suddenly ill
short: First aid: bleeding, burns, breathing, injuries, sudden illness
intro: Readings for first aid until help arrives: checking the person, calling for help, bleeding, burns, breathing and CPR, injuries and sudden illness. Most pages come from the IFRC's international first aid guidelines (2020), written for first aid trainers; some from Austrian and German civil-protection guides.

choices.label: I don't know what's wrong: how do I check the person?
choices.hint: An accident, a collapse, several people hurt

read.label: Check the person, in order
read.note: Is it safe? Does the person respond, is the airway open, are they breathing normally, are they bleeding badly?

read.label: Stay safe, call early, help the worst hurt first
read.note: When to keep away and alert the authorities, calling with the phone on speaker, and several injured people.

read.label: What to tell the emergency services
read.note: Stay calm and answer their questions; better to call early with little information than to wait.

read.label: What a first aider does
read.note: In German. Stay calm, make the place safe, life-saving steps, call for help, what to say.

choices.label: Heavy bleeding, a cut or a wound
choices.hint: Blood soaking through, a deep cut, a dirty graze

read.label: Stop severe bleeding
read.note: Press hard on the wound; a tourniquet only on an arm or leg and only if pressure fails; what not to do.

read.label: Step by step, and what to leave alone
read.note: Press, lie down, call for help, a second dressing on top; leave an object stuck in the wound where it is.

read.label: A pressure bandage in four steps
read.note: In German. For a deep wound that bleeds heavily.

read.label: Clean a cut or a graze
read.note: Rinse with clean tap water and cover it; signs of infection; tetanus.

choices.label: Burn or scald
choices.hint: Fire, hot water, cooking oil, chemicals, electricity

read.label: Cool the burn with running water
read.note: At least ten minutes, ideally twenty; then a moist non-stick dressing; what not to do.

read.label: No ice, and when to call for help
read.note: Why not ice or ice-cold water, and which burns need the emergency services.

read.label: Chemicals in the eye; burns in babies
read.note: Rinse the eye at once with clean water; get medical advice when a baby or a frail person is burnt.

choices.label: Broken bone, sprain or dislocation
choices.hint: A fall, a twisted ankle, a limb that looks wrong

read.label: Treat it as a fracture and keep it still
read.note: Support the limb as you find it, cool it for up to 20 minutes, splint it for a bumpy journey.

read.label: When to call for help
read.note: A lot of pain or swelling, a limb in an odd position; always wrap an ice pack in a cloth.

read.label: Bone and joint injuries
read.note: In German. Keep it still, cover wounds, take off rings and watches early, cool against swelling.

choices.label: Not responding, not breathing normally, or choking
choices.hint: Collapsed, gasping, food stuck in the throat, pulled from the water

read.label: Unresponsive but breathing: the recovery position
read.note: Shout, shake gently, open the airway, check breathing for up to ten seconds, turn the person on the side.

read.label: Not breathing normally: start CPR
read.note: Assume the heart has stopped; push hard and fast, 100 to 120 a minute, about 5 cm deep, 30 compressions to 2 breaths.

read.label: Choking: back blows and abdominal thrusts
read.note: Up to five blows between the shoulder blades, then up to five abdominal thrusts, in turn.

read.label: Unconscious, or not breathing
read.note: In German. Checking, the recovery position, CPR at 30 to 2, and a defibrillator.

choices.label: Pale, cold, sweaty, weak: it could be shock
choices.hint: After heavy bleeding, bad burns or a severe allergy

read.label: Lay the person down and keep them warm
read.note: On the back, legs raised if they are not injured and it helps, no heat loss, call the emergency services.

read.label: The signs of shock
read.note: Pale skin, bluish lips, cool or clammy skin, a fast pulse; a blanket, and something between the person and cold ground.

choices.label: Head, neck or back injury
choices.hint: A fall, a car crash, a blow to the head

read.label: Warning signs after a blow to the head
read.note: When to call the emergency services at once, and watching the person for the next 24 hours.

read.label: A possible spinal injury
read.note: After road crashes or falls from a height: keep the person still, no collar or strapping, always call for help.

read.label: Do not move the person
read.note: Unless they are in danger, and then with two helpers.

choices.label: Too hot or too cold
choices.hint: Heat stroke, a heat wave, shivering, numb white fingers

read.label: Overheated: cool the person down
read.note: Stop and move somewhere cool; cold-water cooling for an adult overheated by exertion; when to call for help.

read.label: Heat exhaustion and heat stroke
read.note: The signs of each, and cooling in cold water for about 15 minutes.

read.label: Hypothermia
read.note: Out of the cold, off with wet clothes, warm the person, a warm sweet drink if they can swallow; always call for help.

read.label: Frostbite
read.note: Rewarm only if care is more than two hours away and it cannot freeze again: warm water at 37 to 39 °C, never a fire or a heater.

choices.label: Severe allergic reaction
choices.hint: Swelling, trouble breathing after a sting, a food or a medicine

read.label: Adrenaline for anaphylaxis
read.note: The person's own auto-injector; a second dose after 5 to 10 minutes if there is no response and no help yet.

read.label: Using an auto-injector, step by step
read.note: Call for help, lie the person down, inject into the outer thigh through thin clothing.

choices.label: Asthma attack
choices.hint: Wheezing, short of breath, the inhaler is not helping

read.label: Help with an asthma attack
read.note: Sitting up, the person's own inhaler, loosening clothing, away from smoke or dust.

read.label: When to call for help
read.note: No inhaler and an attack lasting minutes, an inhaler that does not work, bluish lips, confusion, tiring.

choices.label: Poisoning: swallowed something, or fumes
choices.hint: Cleaning products, too many pills, a button battery, carbon monoxide

read.label: Swallowed poison, or toxic gas
read.note: Stop further exposure; no vomiting, and no milk, water or charcoal unless the poison centre says so; rescue from gas only if it is safe.

read.label: Call the poison centre or the emergency services
read.note: And preventing poisoning at home, including a carbon monoxide detector.

read.label: Carbon monoxide, and button batteries
read.note: Carbon monoxide has no colour or smell; what to do when a button battery is swallowed.

choices.label: Diarrhoea, vomiting or dehydration
choices.hint: A stomach bug, bad water, a baby or an older person drying out

read.label: Drink, or oral rehydration salts
read.note: Mild dehydration: drink enough; severe: oral rehydration salts; keep breastfeeding; when to get help.

read.label: A home-made rehydration drink
read.note: Salt, sugar and drinking water, in the amounts the page gives.

read.label: Stomach pain, diarrhoea and vomiting: when to get care
read.note: Severe diarrhoea, repeated vomiting, a fever over 38 °C, blood in vomit or stools.

choices.label: Chest pain, stroke signs, a seizure or low blood sugar
choices.hint: Crushing chest pain, a drooping face, a fit, a diabetic person acting confused

read.label: Chest pain: a possible heart attack
read.note: Call even if the pain lasted only minutes; aspirin while waiting, unless the person must not take it.

read.label: Stroke: the FAST check
read.note: Face, arms, speech, time: call the emergency services at once and note when it started.

read.label: A seizure: protect the person
read.note: Clear the space, cushion the head, do not hold the person down; when to call for help.

read.label: Low blood sugar
read.note: Glucose or sugar if the person responds and can swallow; call if there is no quick improvement.

choices.label: Bites and stings
choices.hint: A dog bite, a bee sting, a tick, a snake

read.label: Animal bites
read.note: Clean the wound with clean water and soap, against infection and rabies.

read.label: Ticks
read.note: Removing a tick, and the signs after a bite that need a doctor.

read.label: Snakebite
read.note: Keep the person as still as possible and call for help; no tourniquet, cutting or sucking.

choices.label: Help is far away, or many people are hurt
choices.hint: A disaster, phones down, help may take hours or days

read.label: When help may take days
read.note: In disasters, emergency services may take hours, days or weeks: focus on bleeding, the airway and shock.

read.label: Several people hurt
read.note: Call early, call again with details, and care first for those whose lives are in most danger.

read.label: If 112 does not work
read.note: In German. Go to the nearest police station or hospital, if you can.

limits.text: Do not go near the scene if it is not safe.
Call the emergency services for all severe bleeding.
Do not pull out an object stuck in a wound. Once a tourniquet is on, leave it on until help arrives.
Never cover an infected wound: get medical help.
Do not put ice or ice-cold water on a burn.
Call for help for large or deep burns, burns near the face, throat or genitals, and burns from chemicals, electricity or flames.
If breathing is not normal (gasping, irregular or none), start CPR at once.
Do not touch the person while a defibrillator gives a shock.
Do not sweep blindly with a finger in a choking person's mouth.
Do not use abdominal thrusts on a baby.
Call the emergency services at once if a person shows signs of shock.
After a blow to the head, call at once if the person passes out even briefly, vomits more than once, has a seizure, or bleeds from the nose or ears.
Do not move someone who may have a spinal injury unless they are in danger.
Call for help for every case of hypothermia, and do not rub the person's skin.
Always get medical care for frostbite.
After a swallowed poison, do not make the person vomit, and give no milk, water or charcoal unless the poison centre says so.
For chest pain, call the emergency services even if it lasted only a couple of minutes.
If you suspect a stroke, call the emergency services at once and note the time it started.
During a seizure, do not hold the person down.
Do not put a tourniquet on a snakebite.
